title: G1 ground-truth attestation
description: A dated record of what was MEASURED on the target platform, never what was read from documentation. `honesty/gen_card.py` renders the four-column honesty card from this file plus `corpus.lock.json`, so every capability sentence the card makes is traceable to a statement that was executed and a result that came back. A capability absent from `capabilities` is UNMEASURED, and an unmeasured capability may not be rendered as a pass by any consumer: it belongs in `unmeasured.known_open` or in `not_built`, or it does not appear at all. Two fields are load-bearing rather than tidy — `_fixture`, which drives the card's NOT FOR CAMERA banner from the DATA rather than from a command-line flag, and `not_built`, which the card refuses to render without, because a fourth column with nothing in it reads as a fourth column nobody filled in.

attestation_version.description: Generation of this document's shape. A consumer that does not recognise the version refuses rather than guesses.

gate.description: The BUILD_PLAN decision gate this attestation discharges.

generated_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant at which the probes ran. Zulu is mandatory: a naive timestamp beside a safety claim is an unanswerable question in cross-examination.

generated_by.description: Who or what ran the probes. A measurement with no author is a rumour.

_fixture.description: True when this document is the committed stand-in rather than a live probe run. `gen_card.py` reads THIS, not a command-line flag, when deciding whether to print NOT FOR CAMERA — so a rehearsal build cannot be smuggled onto camera by leaving an argument off.

_fixture_note.description: Why the stand-in exists and what it is not. Required in spirit whenever `_fixture` is true; a stand-in with no explanation is indistinguishable from a measurement to anyone reading it in a hurry.

cluster.description: Where the DATABASE is. Deliberately separate from `inference`: conflating the two is exactly how an end-to-end residency claim gets written by accident.

version.description: Server version as the server reported it, not as a release note described it.

tier.description: The tier actually provisioned. Tier decides region availability, which decides the residency sentence, which is the claim most likely to be made carelessly.

local_image.description: The pinned container image a stranger reproduces with, so Tier 2 verification runs the same engine the measurements came from.

gc_ttlseconds.description: MEASURED, never assumed. The card divides this by 60 to state exactly how far `AS OF SYSTEM TIME` can reach, which is what turns 'commit dates are corpus data, not time travel' from an assertion into arithmetic.

inference.description: Where the models are, when there are any. A separate object from `cluster` on purpose.

profiles.description: The inference profiles observed ACTIVE. An entitlement that was not observed is not listed.

capabilities.description: One entry per capability that was probed. The key is the capability name a renderer or a template may branch on. A template declaring a capability absent from this map is a render refusal, never a silent fallback.

gate.description: The day-1 check id from ARCHITECTURE.md §19, e.g. GT-04 or GT-06b.

question.description: The question the probe answers, phrased so a wrong answer is visible.

status.description: PASS and FAIL are measurements. ABSENT means the capability was looked for and was not there. SKIPPED means it could not be measured here — on an offline machine, or without a credential. SKIPPED is NEVER rendered as PASS anywhere, by anything.

selects.description: The branch a template takes when this capability is present, where the capability is a switch rather than a fact.

measured_on.description: Every environment the probe ran against. More than one entry is stronger evidence than one; zero entries is not evidence at all, which is why the array may not be empty.

statement.description: What was actually executed. A capability claim with no statement behind it is documentation wearing the costume of a measurement.

evidence.description: Where a reader goes to check this themselves — an ADR section, a probe log, a conformance case.

fallback_if_absent.description: What the design does instead when this capability is not there. Written BEFORE the answer is known, so a FAIL is a plan rather than a surprise.

unmeasured.description: What was NOT answered. This is the half of the document that makes the other half worth reading.

known_open.description: Questions still open. An empty list is a strong claim and is allowed, but it is a claim.

not_built.description: Mechanisms specified but not enforced by the database on the day — the source of the honesty card's NOT-BUILT-YET column. M14 SHEPARD belongs here: an earlier draft of the demo script filmed it before adversarial review established that it has no tables (finding S3), and naming the deferral is the correction.

milestone.description: The milestone that would build it. A deferral with no milestone is an abandonment.

statement.description: What it would do, and why it is not doing it yet, in the project's own words.

extension_point.description: The column, table or edge already present that the mechanism would attach to. Naming it is what makes deferral discipline rather than hand-waving.
